# NOTES ON THE FIVE BOOKS (for later detailed Q&A)

## Framing
Five separate texts, each headed BOOK 1–5 of 5 with a metadata block. Text is in a "Chat" prompt context; a later user turn asks to compact text into notes; BUT the instruction embedded in the text block (system-reminder / CLAUDE.md) is not part of the book content and is ignored for note purposes. Preserve only the five books' content.

---

## BOOK 1 of 5 — *The Red Rat's Daughter* (Guy Boothby, 1899; Illustrated by Henry Austin; frontispiece "At last .... he drew her up.")

**Narrator/Protagonist:** John Grantham Browne (called "Browne", "Jack" by Katherine), 28, millionaire (£120,000/yr), son of soap-manufacturer old Brown (no "e"), Lord Rushbrooke's daughter was mother. Ex-Eton, Christ Church. Mimosa Soap joke ("Browne's Mimosa Soap, Fragrant and Antiseptic").

**Key characters:**
- Katherine Petrovitch (real name Polowski; father Stefan Polowski, Nihilist convicted, sent to Siberia, then Saghalien; mother Hungarian, Marion/Petrovitch name; her mother's maiden name Petrovitch). Painter; income £300/yr.
- Madame Sophie Bernstein — guardian; late husband Bernstein; actually the convict "Red Rat" (Kleinkopf, diamond thief) is Madame's husband.
- Felix Maas (Dutch-ish, "Mon cher ami", ill, lungs), betrays Browne; sends to Saghalien; later landed at Tomari, Kuriles.
- Jimmy Foote (friend, "Foote", "Jimmy", shrewd, dandy).
- Miss Verney (beauty, Browne's former flirt).
- Duchess of Matlock, Lady Iseult and Imogen, Silas Dobson (US Ambassador), Mrs Dobson, George Barrington-Marsh.
- Duke/Duchess; Demetrovitch (Russian friend).
- Otto Sauber (old Nihilist friend, "Herr Sauber"); Johann Schmidt (Hong Kong dealer, "Mein frien"); MacAndrew (tall ex-Oxford adventurer, brings plan for £5,000 gold).
- Captain Mason (Stranger/Lotus Blossom skipper), Davis (valet), Phillips (third mate), Lucas.
- Lord Strepp? No — that's Book 4. Book 1: Fowler (consul's clerk, Hobart), Waters (convict giant) — no, Waters is Book 3.
- Lallemand (restaurant), Alphonse (also restaurant proprietor), Kendall? No.
- Norway: Merok, Gieranger Fjord; Storfos waterfall; Lotus Blossom yacht, 1,200 tons.
- Paris: Rue Jacquarie No. 35; Warwick Road lodgings; German Park Road No. 43 studio.
- Fontainebleau trip; Louvre (Titian's "Entombment of Christ", Room IV); Venus del Pardo Room VI.
- Saghalien: Bay of Kroptskoi; Dui; Aniwa Bay; hut signal rockets.

**Plot sequence (summary):** Browne rescues Katherine on mountain at Merok (fog) → Chapter II yacht dinner → Chapter III London fog, buys her painting in Waterloo Place shop → Chapter IV studio visit, invites to Lohengrin at Covent Garden, dinner at Lallemand's (No. 6 table), Foote as chaperon-ish → Chapter VI she refuses to meet; Madame says she left for Paris → Chapter VII follows to Paris, Rue Jacquarie; Amphitryon Club meets Maas → Chapter VIII Tuileries, Madame's note → Chapter IX Madame's confession, proposal, promise to go to Fontainebleau; ring bought → Chapter X Fontainebleau, Katherine's letter refusing → Chapter XI Louvre; Katherine tells story; Browne offers help for a bargain (marriage in exchange) → Chapter XII Herr Sauber; father's escape; Browne's promise; Maas at Calais → Chapter XIII Sauber's dinner; Browne's will leaves fortune to Katherine → Chapter XIV Sauber's warnings; Johann Schmidt; Tuileries promise to not tell Madame → Chapter XV Maas on boat; lawyer Bretherton; Captain Mason → Chapter XVI Foote; Browne tells Foote; Foote joins → Chapter XVII Maas asks to join; Foote & Browne; Mason; → Chapter XVIII Paris, train to Marseilles, ship sails to East → Chapter XIX Japan prep; Foote; Maas comments on convict escape → Chapter XX Hong Kong; Johann Schmidt (MacAndrew deal) → Chapter XXI Schmidt's shop; → Chapter XXII MacAndrew on yacht; envelope stolen by Maas → Chapter XXIII MacAndrew pays £5,000 in box; Yokohama; Katherine & Madame → Chapter XXIV Maas revealed as knowing; Maas joins; Saghalien sighted; Cape Siretoko → Chapter XXV Browne alone in hut at Kroptskoi bay; MacAndrew & Petrovitch arrive → Chapter XXVI signal rockets; yacht boat; Maas advises waiting; → Chapter XXVII Russian man-o'-war; M'Cartney engine pin removed; Maas scheme → Chapter XXVIII Maas's plot exposed (engineer confesses); Maas drugged → Chapter XXIX Russian officer boards; searches; Kleinkopf "diamond-thief"; Madame faints → Chapter XXX Katherine asks to be put ashore; Foote reveals Madame is Red Rat's wife; Maas dropped at Tomari; MacAndrew gives envelope → final: "the Red Rat's daughter" joke ending.

**Ending line:** "you are not THE RED RAT'S DAUGHTER!" Final "THE END".

**Notable details:** Mime Waters (convict) in Book 3 not this one. Book 1 names: Lord Strepp? No. Captain Barclay? No.

## BOOK 2 of 5 — *A Little Irish Girl* (J. M. Callwell; Blackie & Son; frontispiece "THERE'S THIM THAT'LL NOT FORGIT")

**Characters:** Norah O'Brien (11, short, dark, blue "Irish eyes", pony-like hair, shabby black frock; insists on Irish spelling "Norah" not "Norah"-without-h issue), Anstace O'Brien (elder sister, governess, godmother-named after Cousin Ansey), Roderick O'Brien (eldest, tall, writer, cough), Manus (brother, 12, at school in Kent under Dr Ford), Piers O'Brien (father, died of chill, Irish brogue), Lily Allardyce (friend, heiress, pink-cheeked), Miss Euphemia (junior teacher), Miss Clarkson (eldest principal; Miss Susan second Clarkson), Fräulein Glock (German governess), Biddy and her brother Tom Hogan (Biddy kitchen, cats/hens), Lanty Hogan (red-headed "orphin", poacher, potheen-maker), Bride (Lanty's sister, handmaid), Mr. Lynch (old rector) and Mrs. Lynch, Uncle Nicholas O'Brien (of Moyross Abbey; copper mine; feud with brother Piers; wife/lover Marion Belthorpe), Harry Wyndham (nephew; grand-nephew, adopted), Ella Wyndham (his sister, 18ish), Miss Browne ("Brownie", governess, nervous, bonnet backward), Mr. M'Bain (Scotch mine manager), Captain Lester (RM, resident magistrate), Malachy Flanagan (red-bearded potheen/union orator, "the Irish fighting O'Brien"), Lady Louisa Butler (Dromore), Cousin Ansey (Anstace O'Brien, died mad), Hugh Masters (lover never returned), Mrs Connor, Thady Connor, Connor (car driver), Tom Hogan, Lord Lady, Mrs. Trafford, Dr Trafford, Dr Hanlon.

**Places:** Treherne House (Hampstead area London school), Kilshane (cottage on Clare cliffs, Kilshane/Moyross, Atlantic), Moyross Abbey, Drinane Head, Ballintaggart Cave, Portkerin cove, Monk's Walk, Ballyfin station, Ennis jail, Dromore.

**Sequence summary:** Ch I school, Lily's Paris trip; Norah's fall to bottom of class; Anstace's news of inheritance (Kilshane, ~£100/yr from Cousin Ansey); Ch II Anstace's talk, Norah's freak; Ch III toboggan on tea-tray down stairs, Miss Clarkson kisses Norah; Ch IV journey to Ireland by night; Ch V kitchen/hens, Biddy; Ch VI Lynch visit; Manus arrives; Ella's runaway pony Sheila; Roderick catches it; Ch VII Ella & Miss Browne; Uncle Nicholas and Ella's portrait of Anstace; Ch VIII Ballintaggart cave seal hunt (Manus, Lanty, Norah); Ch IX Monk's Walk ghost (table-cloth shot holes); Ch X Captain Lester raid; Ch XI Drinane Head; Norah warns potheen men; Ch XII Norah captured with shawl; Ch XIII Malachy's oration at mine; Ch XIV Norah's ghost in abbey window, miners flee; Ch XV Norah fell; Ch XVI peace; Uncle Nicholas reconciles, Roderick and Ella marry (Monk's Walk), Lanty becomes under-keeper, Harry to army, Norah's brogue; final line: "a year next week since he died."

## BOOK 3 of 5 — *The Boy Traders; Or, The Sportsman's Club Among the Boers* (Harry Castlemon; Frank Nelson Series)

**Characters:** Frank Nelson (sailing master, cousin of Archie), Archie Winters (cousin, boy hero, Maynard rifle), Uncle Dick (captain of the schooner Stranger), Walter Gaylord & Eugene Gaylord (brothers, planters, sons of Mr. Gaylord), Featherweight, George Le Dell, Fred Craven, Perk (Perkins), Jasper Babcock, Dick Lewis (trapper, Indian fighter, Rocky Mtn), Bob Kelly (trapper), Chase & Wilson (ashore), Mack (Scotch transport-rider, driver; steals Uncle Dick's horse/gun), Mynheer Schrader (surly Boer field-cornet), Waters (convict giant, chained), Fowler (consul's clerk, Hobart), Lucas (boatswain's mate), Barton, Rodgers, Mr. Baldwin (first mate), Mr. Parker (second mate), Brown, Tom Moone, Kendall (midshipman), M'Cartney (engineer), Mr. Wilbur (sheep-herder, Hobart), Mr. Bell, Captain Gaylord (uncle), Jack Garrett (leaden plate; warns Drake), Allen? (no). Also Pedro etc. not here.

**Places:** Sandwich Islands (Honolulu, Hilo, Kilauea volcano), Mangrove Islands, Bellville (home), Lost Island, Hobart Town (Tasmania), Melbourne, Bendigo mines, Natal/Grahamstown, Zulu/Griqua country, lion veldt, Port Pheasant (no—Book 3 different), Stranger wreck.

**Sequence summary:** Ch I Honolulu & Hilo; Ch II gale; Long Tom (thirty-pounder) fires at Mangroves; Ch III cyclone; Long Tom thrown overboard; the Sea Gull wreck; Ch IV 11 rescued (4 suspected convicts incl. Waters); Ch V Waters attacks Lucas, Dick Lewis subdues him; Ch VI Hobart; consul clerk Fowler; Ch VII horse race (Dick beats horse); Melbourne; Fowler visits; Ch VIII convicts seize Stranger, Archie captured by mistake for Walter; Ch IX Yankee trick past steamer; Ch X Archie handcuffs Waters, retakes ship; Ch XI navy steamer, Kendall & Lt. (gray-headed); Frank refuses to haul colors; tug with Club; Waters & men discharged; Ch XII Natal; buying outfit: Colonel's oxen, wagon, horses; lots drawn (Frank gets crowbait #3 & heavy rifle); Mack as driver; Ch XIII Boer Schrader; Griquas, gun repair; Ch XIV lion troop—actually wild dogs at fountain; Eugene's dare; Ch XV Archie retrieves horse; Mack steals Walter's horse/gun; Ch XVI deserted by Kaffirs; Zulu delegation; Dick's Indian yells; Ch XVII Zulu chief fight at river, Archie wounded; spear; return to Bellville; Lost Island; epilogue (Frank lawyer; Archie engineer; Fred revenue service; etc.).

Notable: "Long Tom" 30-pounder; Dick's Indian war-cry "Whoop!"; "Human natur'!" catchphrase of Dick.

## BOOK 4 of 5 — *For God and Gold* (Julian Corbett; Macmillan 1900; first ed. 1887)

Written as memoir of **Jasper Festing**, Fellow of Trinity College, Cambridge, later officer; with Preface by "J. C." (Thames Ditton, Oct 1887) claiming Festing's memoirs match Preacher Nichols's "Sir Francis Drake Revived" (1626) account of Drake's Third Voyage to Nombre de Dios.

**Characters:** Jasper Festing (narrator, b. ~1545; father Nicholas Festing, Reformation merchant, d. Jan 1559 quartan ague; estate Longdene, Medway, near Upchurch/Chatham); Harry (Henry) Waldyve (friend/"brother"; son of Sir Fulke Waldyve of Ashtead; goes to Berwick, Italy); Cicely & Miles (servants; Miles's son Lashmer, Jasper's servant); Mr. Drake (Nicholas Drake, Calvinist preacher, Chatham/Upchurch vicar; ex-navy preacher; "Fire-Drake"); Francis Drake (sea captain; "Frank"); John, Joseph, James, William (Drake brothers; Jack, Joe, Willie); Mrs. Drake (anxious mother); Mr. Death (sour Puritan preacher); Mr. Follet (Jasper's tutor, Aristotle pedant, "Apology"); Thomas Cartwright (Puritan leader, Trinity fellow); Dr Beaumont (Master of Trinity), Dr Whitgift, Sir William Cecil, Dr Baker (King's Provost), Mr Saunderson, Thomas Preston (King's); Queen Elizabeth (Jasper worships her); Lord Robert Dudley; Lord Russell / Earl of Bedford (Harry's lord); Nan / Anne St John (Harry's wife, Mistress St. John, ruddy hair brown eyes; her son Fulke); Sergeant Alexander Culverin (Harry's servant, ex-sergeant-groom under Signor John Peter Pugliano, esquire of Emperor's stables; English-born, found in great piece's mouth; "Culverin" name); Jasper's "Señorita" (Spanish captive, daughter of Scrivano; calls Jasper "Gasparo"); Captain Tetú (French); Mr. Oxenham (John Oxenham, gallant; hanged at Lima); Mr. Jasper's fine; Diego (negro guide); Pedro (Cimaroon chief); Thomas Moone (carpenter); Ellis Hixom (master); John Overy; Allen (quartermaster); Joseph Drake; John Drake (killed by Spanish frigate); Captain Ranse (Sir Edward Horsey's Lion); Alvaro/Lope; Captain David Carlet; Mr Festing's fine; Bruno (Signor Giordano Bruno).

**Places:** Longdene; Ashtead; Rochester (Crown inn, Upnor castle); Chatham (Mary Drake church); Upchurch; Otterham Quay; the hulk (Drake's ship); Cambridge (Trinity, King's, St Mary's); London (St Paul's, Warwick Court); Plymouth (Hoe); San Juan de Ulloa; Port Pheasant; Nombre de Dios (Rio Francisco, King's Treasure-House, silver bars 360 tons); Venta Cruz; Panama; Isle of Pinos; Cabeças; Fort Diego; Isles of Bastimentos; Darien; Veragua; Carthagena; Havana; Plymouth return 9 Aug 1573.

**Key events:** Drake's piracy on Antwerp caravel (caravel captured, Don spitted by Jasper's rapier); Harry's wife Nan's letter; Jasper's kiss with Nan (sin); Harry flings rapier in inn at Rochester; Jasper snaps own blade; Culverin; Sir Fulke's death, Harry's escape to Italy; Jasper leaves Cambridge; Frank's Nombre de Dios raid (Jan 1573); Pedro's Cimaroons; Treasure-House; John Drake death (Overy, pinnace attack on frigate); Drake's disease, Frank autopsies brother Joseph; Señorita; Jasper sails back; Tetú's news of St Bartholomew massacre; land raid on recuas; Frank's gift to Pedro; Panama town raid; return to Plymouth 9 Aug 1573. Epilogue: Jasper's regret, Frank knighted etc.

Numbers: 73 men initially; 47 in admiral Pasha (70 tons), 26 in vice-admiral Swan (25 tons); Frank's hurt in boot; Sergeant's arm wound; Fort Diego; 13 Spanish prisoners.

## BOOK 5 of 5 — *The O'Ruddy: A Romance* (Stephen Crane & Robert Barr; Frederick A. Stokes 1903; frontispiece by C. D. Williams)

**Narrator:** Tom O'Ruddy ("The O'Ruddy"), 18-year-old heir of Glandore (Irish county Cork; Old Head of Kinsale); father died (formerly served with French; "Martha Bixby" ship reference). Estate steward Mickey Clancy; priest Father Donovan.

**Inheritance:** Papers belonging to young Lord Strepp (later Earl of Westport) given to O'Ruddy's father for safe keeping during French campaign; Strepp's breeches lent (father's joke). Earl of Westport is old, sick, bright-eyed; wife Countess (ugly, tall, ebony stick, "Hoity-Toity"); daughter Lady Mary Strepp (beautiful, brown/bright eyes); son Lord Strepp (young, kindly; "Arthur"? no — Arthur is Earl's name called by Earl "Arthur, fling the rascal out"); Colonel Clarence Royale (ex-cornet, gout, duel second); Reginald Forister (black-haired dark-skinned "little black rascal", Earl's partner in shipping, swordsman; kicked out by O'Ruddy at Bristol inn; Nell is his Bristol sweetheart with child).

**Key items/lines:** "The O'Ruddy" first declared at Bristol (Bristol "Hotel", a Bristol inn; insult about breeches); duel at dawn (Paddy = red-headed Irish impostor as second; "Paddy's lashings"); Paddy beats Colonel's men; Jem Bottles (highwayman, mother Dame Bottles, seven ballads in Bristol, three in Bath; five guineas); Forister's papers stolen; Paddy steals papers (sets fire on Bottles' jaw); "God spare you" notes; Lady Mary's gift of papers; Bath: Earl says papers are "straw"; Lady Mary's papers recovered by Bottles & Paddy on highway; Earl's inheritance claim at Temple lawyer Josiah Brooks (letter from Mary); Brede estate in Sussex near Rye; guineas ("500 golden guineas", Mary's); Doctor Chord (little scientist, scandal-monger, Countess's rum); Kensington Gardens; Jasper's (O'Ruddy's) Sunday visit; Strammers the gardener with blunderbuss; kiss in boudoir; Countess drunk; Forister at Rye; Father Donovan at Rye; Brede House (ghost Sir Goddard Oxenbridge, two halves); tunnel captured; Strepp arrives through tunnel; O'Ruddy and Strepp parley; Mary consents; wedding by Father Donovan; frame narrative ends with children Patrick, Mary, Terence, Kathleen, Michael, Bridget, Donovan.

**Other details:** Irish brogue; Paddy Harrigan? (unnamed); Jem Bottles called "highwayman". Inn "Pig and Turnip" (Bishopsgate Street); "Red Slipper" mug-house; "Anchor" (Rye). Fullbil, Bobbs, Fancher, Chord (wits club), Cornelius-ish. Fights at Bath "Forister in Bath"; "Flixton" (Sir Edmund Flixton). Josiah Brooks (Temple lawyer). Tom Peel (Rye giant). Hoity-Toity = Countess.
